refnamediv.refpurpose: Set timeout period on a stream

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
boolstream_set_timeout resourcestream intseconds intmicroseconds0
Sets the timeout value on stream, expressed in the sum of seconds and microseconds.
The timeout applies to each wait for data to read and for room to write, not to a whole read or write. A new socket stream starts with the value of default_socket_timeout at the time it was created: changing the setting later does not affect open streams, and an accepted socket takes the current timeout of its listening socket.
When the stream times out, the 'timed_out' key of the array returned by stream_get_meta_data is set to &true;. A read timeout generates no error or warning, whereas a write timeout on a socket emits an E_NOTICE and fwrite returns &false; or a short count.

&reftitle.parameters;
stream
The target stream.
seconds
The seconds part of the timeout to be set. It is added to microseconds, which carry into the seconds when above 999999. A negative value, or a value above 2147482, means no timeout: reads wait until data is available. 0 (with no microseconds) means no wait at all.
microseconds
The microseconds part of the timeout to be set. The resolution of the timeout is one millisecond: a value below 1000 is rounded down.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
&return.success; &false; is returned for streams that have no timeout, such as plain files and the php://memory, php://temp, php://output, php://input and data: streams, directory handles, or pipes (from popen and proc_open, and STDIN unless it is a socket), without any error. It returns &true; for TCP, UDP and Unix domain sockets.
